name: Demand Management
description: Screen, assess and recommend on incoming demands. Validates each demand first; if it fails validation, the assessment does not proceed.

item_fields.name: demand_id
item_fields.label: Demand ID
item_fields.description: The unique number of the demand, written as D-YYYY-NNN (for example D-2026-004). It is given once when the request is registered and never reused. Every other sheet refers to the demand by this ID.

item_fields.name: date_submitted
item_fields.label: Date submitted
item_fields.description: The date the request was registered. It is used to order demands and to compare similar requests.

item_fields.name: department
item_fields.label: Requesting department
item_fields.description: The department that asks for the change and will use the result. Pick it from the list. It is the business domain, not an architecture domain.

item_fields.name: requester_role
item_fields.label: Requester role
item_fields.description: The job role of the person who submitted the request, for example Payroll Manager. Write a role, never a personal name.

item_fields.name: sponsor
item_fields.label: Business sponsor
item_fields.description: The role that owns the benefit and stands behind the request, for example Chief Financial Officer. The sponsor confirms the need, the deadline and the benefit. It can differ from the requester.

item_fields.name: title
item_fields.label: Demand title
item_fields.description: A short name for the demand that says what is wanted, for example "Complaint tracking system".

item_fields.name: business_need
item_fields.label: Business need / problem
item_fields.description: What is wrong or missing today, in the requester's own words. Describe the problem and who is affected, not the solution.

item_fields.name: expected_outcome
item_fields.label: Expected outcome / benefit
item_fields.description: What will be better after the change, with numbers if known (hours saved, errors avoided, people served).

item_fields.name: request_type
item_fields.label: Request type
item_fields.description: The kind of request, picked from the list: New solution, Enhancement of existing, Interface between systems, Data & analytics, Infrastructure & platform, Licence or renewal, Support issue, Other. It helps the first sorting only. The architecture domain is decided later.

item_fields.name: requester_urgency
item_fields.label: Requester urgency
item_fields.description: The requester's own view of how urgent it is. Critical: a service is stopped, or a legal or mandated deadline is within 3 months. High: a deadline or significant risk within 6 months. Medium: a clear benefit with a deadline within 12 months. Low: nice to have, no deadline. The agent sets its own urgency in screening, so this field may be changed.

item_fields.name: urgency_reason
item_fields.label: Reason for urgency / deadline
item_fields.description: What drives the date and what happens if it is late, for example a mandate, an audit finding or a service failure. It is optional, but without it the agent cannot confirm a Critical or High urgency.

item_fields.name: target_go_live
item_fields.label: Target go-live
item_fields.description: The date the requester wants the solution in use. It is compared with the delivery calendar and with other projects.

item_fields.name: systems_mentioned
item_fields.label: Systems or data mentioned
item_fields.description: The systems, tools or data the request involves, named as the requester knows them, for example "HR app, payroll, attendance devices". The agent matches these names to the Application Catalog and the Data Catalog.

validation.fail_message: Not a valid demand — returned to requester for clarification.
questions: Is this a true demand (a need or change), not an incident or a question?
Is there a clear business need or outcome?
Is there enough detail to assess it (what / who / why)?

stages.name: Screening & Impact Assessment
stages.instructions: Screen each demand and assess its impact, filling the columns below. First decide whether it is a true demand. If it is not (not yet complete, an incident, or a standard service), answer only what can still be answered and write Not assessed in the other columns. Use Not applicable where a step does not apply to this kind of demand, None where you checked and found nothing, and No link found or Not identified where a link or capability could not be found. Answer only what the knowledge base supports; for anything it does not, say what is needed rather than guessing.

columns.name: Is it a true demand?
columns.description: Yes, or Not yet: return for information when the request is incomplete, or the type of not-a-demand (for example No: incident, No: standard service).
columns.activity: Checking each demand is a true demand

columns.name: Demand type
columns.description: Digital, Technical or People. Not assessed when the demand is not a true demand.

columns.name: Domain
columns.description: Architecture domains, main one first: Business, Data, Application, Integration, Technology, Security. A technical demand is Application, Data, Technology or Security. A people demand has no domain: write Not applicable.
columns.collate:
4. Add Security when the data is Confidential or Restricted (check the Data Classification Standard; the Data classification is decided before this property, use it), or the demand touches sign-in, encryption or security controls.
5. Record the business domain (the department that asks) separately, not in this field.
columns.rules:
Valid domains and what each covers (exactly five):
• Business: processes, services, policies, organization, capabilities and people
• Data: any area that comes under the data domain in TOGAF and similar frameworks, for example data sources, analytics, reports, data quality, data sharing and data classification
• Application: any area that comes under the application, system and platform domain in TOGAF and similar frameworks, for example applications for business users, and the interfaces and integration between applications, modules and system features
• Technology: any area that comes under the infrastructure and technology domain in TOGAF and similar frameworks, for example infrastructure, cloud, hosting, network, data center and similar
• Security: a new or changed security control or security capability. Controls can be sign-in and access, encryption, monitoring or protection of Confidential or personal data (for example, multi-factor sign-in for the staff portal)
Main domain first. Integration is not a domain: interfaces and integration belong to Application. Business domains (Human Resources, Finance, Customer Services and others) are not values of this field.
columns.how_to_resolve:
1. Read the business need, the expected outcome, and the systems and data mentioned in the demand.
2. Check each named system, data set and platform against the Application Catalog, Data Catalog, Technology Catalog and Security Control Catalog to see which domain it belongs to.
3. Choose the main domain and write it first, based on the majority of the content. Add other domains only when the demand clearly needs them.

columns.name: Urgency
columns.description: Critical, High, Medium or Low. Set from the deadline and what happens if it is missed. Not assessed when the demand is not a true demand.
columns.how_to_resolve: Read the deadline and what happens if it is missed from the demand text. If the demand states neither, answer needs_input and say so.

columns.name: Priority
columns.description: Fast-track, Standard or Backlog, from the weighted score of the prioritization model. No score when the demand is not assessed.
columns.how_to_resolve: Apply the EA prioritization rule to the demand. The rule has not been supplied yet: if it is not available to you, answer needs_input and say the prioritization rule is required.

columns.name: Mandate / business or DT objective
columns.description: Objective and initiative IDs from the strategy, and any mandate. Write No link found if none.
columns.info_needed: The objective, initiative ID or mandate this demand supports, or confirmation that there is none.

columns.name: Linked initiative or project
columns.description: Initiative or project IDs from the roadmap and the initiative list. Write No link found if none.
columns.info_needed: The initiative or project ID from the roadmap this demand belongs to, or confirmation that there is none.

columns.name: Impacted business capability
columns.description: Capability names from the business architecture. Write Not identified if none.
columns.info_needed: The business capability this demand affects.

columns.name: Impacted application
columns.description: Names with IDs from the application inventory or the contract register.
columns.info_needed: The application (with its ID) this demand affects.
columns.collate:
Link by a name match (through the catalogue). Never link by department alone. A solution that does not exist yet is not listed here.

1. Read the systems and data named in the demand and in the answers to the intake questions.
2. Match each name to the Application Catalog, using the glossary and aliases (for example, 'the HR app' is the Peoplex HR system, C-204).
3. Add applications that exchange data with the matched ones when the demand needs that data. Use the graph relationships read for each name, and the Application Interaction Diagram, Data Flow Diagram and Data to Application Matrix where they were retrieved.
4. List the main application first, with its catalog ID or contract ID.
5. In your note, describe how the application links to the other artefacts and components (Data Catalog, Application to Technology Matrix, Application to Security Control Matrix), so that the Screening observation can use it.

columns.name: Is duplicate
columns.description: Whether another demand in the sheet or an existing artefact already covers the same need.
columns.how_to_resolve: Compare this demand with the other demands in the same request sheet, and with nothing else. Yes when another demand in the sheet asks for the same outcome, for the same users, on the same systems, even if it is worded differently; No when the comparison found none; Not assessed when a demand could not be compared. A match needs the same need and the same systems, not the same words.
columns.collate:
Two demands are the same when they ask for the same outcome, for the same users, on the same systems, even if they are worded differently.
• Related demands with a different outcome are not duplicates. Mention them in your note; the Screening observation writes them up.

columns.name: Owners
columns.description: The roles accountable for the capabilities, applications, data, platforms and security controls that the demand impacts. They confirm the impact and receive the demand for review. Roles only, never personal names.
columns.how_to_resolve:
1. For each impacted application, take the owner role from the Application Catalog or the contract owner role in the contract register.
2. For each impacted capability or service, take the owner role from the Business Capability Map or the Business Service Catalog. If there is none, use the owner of its business domain in the routing matrix.
3. For impacted data, platforms and security controls, take the owner role from the Data Catalog, the Technology Catalog and the Security Control Catalog.
columns.where_to_look:
• Application Catalog: the owner role of each application
• Business Capability Map and Business Service Catalog: the owner role of each capability and service
• Data Catalog: the data owner and steward
• Technology Catalog: the platform owner
• Security Control Catalog: the control owner
• Organization Structure: units and roles, when an owner role is missing
• Initiative portfolio: 'Project manager role (optional)'
columns.rules:
Which owner takes precedence (proposed):
• The application owner decides on the application.
• The capability owner decides on the process and the service.
• The data owner decides on the data, and the platform owner decides on the platform.
• The architecture domain owners review the design. They do not replace the business owner.
List only owners the retrieved evidence names. Capability and service owners are listed only if a retrieved passage names them. The demand coordinator confirms the owners afterwards.
columns.examples:
Correct: 'HR Systems Lead (C-204); Lead Application Architect; Lead Security Architect' for the employee mobile app (the data is Confidential).
Wrong: a personal name, or 'HR Department' (a team, not a role).
columns.info_needed_source: [PROPOSED by Claude] An owner role is missing from the catalog. Write 'owner not in data' and ask the Head of EA Office. The original had no needs-source line.

stages.name: Recommendation
stages.instructions: Check overlap with existing solutions (components, platforms, applications, APIs, prior or running initiatives) and with other demands (consolidate). Check the contract register for licences and renewals that could cover it. Confirm the security fit before recommending reuse. Decide the way forward and the owner, and name the risks and the next steps. The last two properties are the recommendation to the requester: each demand's own section, then one overview of the whole request. They are written only after all the others are done, from them and from the screening. Do NOT recommend new business capabilities. Answer only what the knowledge base supports; for anything it does not, say what is needed.

columns.name: Recommendation type
columns.description:
The way forward for this demand, as one of the five words below. Choose the one that fits what the other answers of this phase show.

Reuse: something we already own meets the need as it is; the demand uses it and nothing changes.
Enhancement: something we already own would meet the need with a change to it (a new feature or an extension).
Merge/CR: the demand covers the same need as another demand in this request, or as work already running; it is combined with that one, or handled as a change request on it, instead of being raised on its own.
Link new artefacts: the need is not met as it is, but what it adds relates to artefacts that exist (applications, data, capabilities, contracts); register what is new and link it to them.
Onboard new requirement: nothing we own or have in flight covers it and there is nothing to combine it with; take it in as a new requirement.
columns.how_to_resolve: Decide from what is already decided for this demand: what it overlaps with, any demand to consolidate with, the contract and licence match and the security fit. Another demand with the same need: Merge/CR. An existing solution that covers the need as it is: Reuse. One that covers it with a change: Enhancement. Overlap with artefacts that exist, with new ones to register: Link new artefacts. No overlap and nothing to combine with: Onboard new requirement. If the overlap is not settled, do not choose by guessing: answer needs_input and say what is needed. Never choose Reuse while the security fit is open.

columns.name: Overlaps with
columns.description: Existing solutions this demand overlaps with: applications, platforms, components, APIs and prior or running initiatives, main one first, each with its catalogue or contract ID. None when you checked and found no overlap.
columns.how_to_resolve: Start from what the screening decided for this demand: the impacted applications and any duplicate with an existing artefact. Add an existing solution only when it serves the same need for the same users, not when it shares a word with the demand. Name each as the catalogue names it, with its ID. A solution that does not exist yet is not listed. If nothing was found, write None; if the catalogue could not be checked, say what is needed.

columns.name: Consolidate with demand(s)
columns.description: Other demands in this request that should be handled together with this one because they ask for the same need, for the same users, on the same systems. Their demand IDs, or None.
columns.how_to_resolve: Compare this demand with the screening answers of the other demands in this request (the duplicate answers, the impacted applications and the impacted capabilities), which are listed for you. Write only demand IDs that appear in this request, never one invented or taken from outside it. A match needs the same need and the same systems, not the same words. None when no other demand matches. If the screening left the duplicate question open, say that instead of writing None.

columns.name: Contract / licence match
columns.description: Whether a contract or licence in the contract register already covers this need, with its contract ID and the renewal or end date where the register gives one. None found when the register was checked and nothing matches.
columns.how_to_resolve: Look in the contract register for the overlapping solutions and the systems the demand names. Give the contract ID and the dates only as the register states them. Do not infer a licence scope from the product's name. None found when it was checked and nothing matches; if the register could not be checked, say what is needed.

columns.name: Security fit
columns.description: Whether the existing solution, or the approach the demand takes, fits the security controls that apply, in one or two plain sentences, and what is still to be confirmed. This is a general fit; the detailed assessment is with the security and infrastructure teams.
columns.how_to_resolve: Build on the screening's data classification and linked security capabilities for this demand. Say what fits and what is not yet confirmed. Do not declare a solution secure on its own: where the sources do not settle it, answer needs_source and say which control or standard has to be checked.

columns.name: Recommended owner
columns.description: The role that should own this demand from here: the owner role of the main solution or capability it overlaps with. A role only, never a personal name.
columns.how_to_resolve: Take the owner role from the screening's Owners answer and from the catalogue entry of the main overlapping solution. Write a role, never a name. If no solution overlaps, take the owner role of the capability the demand impacts. If no role is recorded, say what is needed.

columns.name: Risks and conditions
columns.description: What could stop or change this recommendation, one item per line: what is not yet confirmed, what must be true before it goes ahead, and what it depends on. Each item says who has to confirm it, as a role.
columns.how_to_resolve: Take them from what is open in this assessment: a security fit that is not confirmed, a contract or licence that was not checked, an overlapping solution whose status is unclear (for example one listed as not in use), a dependency on something that is only proposed or has no initiative ID, and anything the screening left open. One short line each, with the ID of the solution or contract it concerns. Do not add a risk that none of the answers or sources supports. None when nothing is open.

columns.name: Next steps
columns.description: What happens next, in order, one item per line, each with the role that does it. Where the requester has something to do, that step says so.
columns.how_to_resolve: Write the steps that follow from the recommendation type and from the risks above: confirming a status with an owner, a review by the security team, a contract check, combining with another demand, raising a change request. Each names a role taken from the Owners answer or from the Recommended owner, never a person's name. Order them so the first one unblocks the rest. Do not invent a process, a date or a team; if no owner is recorded, say whose confirmation is needed. For a demand that should be combined with another, the first step is to continue under that demand.

columns.name: Handled with
columns.description: Whether this demand is handled together with others in the request, and which of them leads. Worked out in code, not by the model: from the consolidation answers, an item named in either direction is linked, and the earliest submitted demand leads. It reads "Alone", or "Combined with D-2026-003; lead: D-2026-001".
columns.activity: Working out which demands are handled together

columns.name: Recommendation
columns.description: This demand's section of the recommendation to the requester: 100 to 150 words, in plain language, written to the requester as "you". It is a draft for the architect to read, edit and approve as part of the request's one recommendation.
columns.how_to_resolve:
You are a senior enterprise architect writing the architecture team's recommendation to the requester. Lead with the decision. Weigh what is gained and what is risked, say what you would not do and why, and be direct about what is not settled. Use judgement where it follows from the answers; do not state a fact that is not in them. Write in plain language that someone who is not an architect can follow: no jargon, and no catalogue codes except the IDs the answers give.

Write this demand's section only, 100 to 150 words, to the requester, from the architecture team. Use only what this assessment found for this demand and, where "Handled with" says it is combined, for the demands it is combined with. Plain text only, with no symbols or markdown. Write these parts as short paragraphs. The first has no heading; each of the others has a short heading on a line of its own:
1. The recommendation (no heading): this demand's recommendation type and what to do, in one or two sentences. If the demand is handled with others, say so first. For the lead: which demands are combined into it and what that changes. For any other: that it should not be raised on its own, and that the work continues under the lead, named.
2. Why: two or three sentences: what it overlaps with, the contract and licence match, and the security fit, with the IDs exactly as the answers give them. Add, from the screening, whatever bears on the way forward: the deadline and urgency, the data classification, and any conflict with the architecture principles and standards.
3. Risks and conditions: from the property of that name, at most two lines.
4. Next steps: from the property of that name, a numbered list of at most three.

Say plainly what is not yet confirmed. Do not add a fact, an ID, a date, a name, a cost or a regulation that is not in the answers or the sources. Do not recommend new business capabilities. Write roles, never personal names. Do not state a grade or a confidence level. If the recommendation type is not decided, say what is needed instead of writing the section.

columns.name: Request overview
columns.description: The opening of the request's recommendation: how the request as a whole should be handled, in plain language, written to the requester. The demands' own sections follow it.
columns.how_to_resolve:
You are a senior enterprise architect writing the architecture team's recommendation to the requester. Lead with the decision. Weigh what is gained and what is risked, say what you would not do and why, and be direct about what is not settled. Use judgement where it follows from the answers; do not state a fact that is not in them. Write in plain language that someone who is not an architect can follow: no jargon, and no catalogue codes except the IDs the answers give.

Write 60 to 120 words of plain text, with no symbols or markdown, to the requester, from the architecture team. Say how many demands the request holds and the overall recommendation, in a sentence or two. Name which demands are handled together and which one leads each group. If the demands should be done in an order, or share a risk or a step, say which and why. Use only the answers shown for the demands of this request. Do not repeat the demands' sections; they follow. Say plainly what is not yet confirmed. Do not add a fact, an ID, a date, a name, a cost or a regulation that is not in the answers or the sources. Do not recommend new business capabilities. Write roles, never personal names. Do not state a grade or a confidence level. If the recommendation type is not decided, say what is needed instead of writing the section.
